text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Parliament accepted in the first reading the amendments to the law on pensions.
- President Guntis Ulmanis granted amnesty to 11 of the 101 prisoners who had applied for amnesty.
- On May 14 the state budget deficit was 1.312 million lats, Latvia's external debt was more than 238 million lats, and its internal debt was 178 million lats.
- The Latvian delegation headed by Minister of Transport Vilis Krishtopans is on a visit in Belarus to discuss issues concerning the tranist of the country's goods through Latvia.
- Parliament rejected an opposition proposal to launch a no-confidence motion against the government.
- Norwegian media group P4 is looking at Radio SWH as a possible investment object.
- Representatives from 24 countries are expected to attend the Baltic Transit Gateway conference in Riga and Ventspils on May 21-22.
- The privatization agency decided to allow Lattelekom to buy the state's share in Latvijas Mobilais Telefons, which is the biggest operator of mobile communications in Latvia.
- Lithuania's central bank outlines its blue print for leaving the currency board system.
- Estonia hopes to become a major tourist destination.
